Article 44
Services for handling complaints of victims of violence against women and children are implemented by:
a. Hospitals.
b. Community health centers.
c. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A)
d. Women and Children Service Unit (UPPA)
e. Trauma Center Shelter (RPTC)
f. Children's Social Shelter (RPSA)
g. Women Crisis Centre (WCC)
h. Marriage Advisory, Development and Preservation Agency (BP4)
i. Police
j. Prosecutor's Office
k. Legal Aid Institute (LBH) and
l. Child Protection Institute.

Article 41
(1) Complaints of acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of victims, families, the community and/or community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may file complaints:
a. Directly.
b. By telephone; and
c. By letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 43 are also authorized to handle victims of violence against women and children based on other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding procedures for providing services for handling complaints as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 50
(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services constitute actions by law enforcement apparatus to implement laws and regulations in the context of handling cases of violence against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
(2) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

CHAPTER XI
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 59
(1) Guidance for the implementation of protection of women and children is carried out by the Regional Government.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out in the form of:
a. Providing training for government apparatus and law enforcers regarding the prevention and handling of violence.
b. Providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children.
c. Providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at Community Health Centers, integrated service units and General Hospitals.
d. Providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence, and
e. Conducting professional improvement for officers, managers of violence case data against women and children at community health centers, integrated service units and General Hospitals.

6. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
7. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and Parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children.
8. Children's Forum is a Children's Participation Forum formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly which are implemented with the consent and willingness of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
9. 14. 15. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families and the community.
16. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
17. Law enforcement is action by officials given authority by the state to implement laws and regulations.

Article 43
Paragraph (1) Sufficiently Clear.
Paragraph (2)
Point a
What is meant by Gender Responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and can carry out empowerment of victims.
Point b
What is meant by Non-Discrimination is that every woman and child without exception has the right to receive services related to the violence they experience; no one may be rejected or given priority over others except on the basis of certain emergency considerations.
Point c
What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing their beliefs, values, and social status.
Point d
What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only by people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.
Point e
What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service providers must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.
Point f
What is meant by respecting individual differences (individual differences) is that each individual must be viewed as unique; each person has a different background and life experience so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any matter.
Point g
What is meant by not judging is that service providers must ensure that whatever the victim's condition or information that comes from the victim will not be assessed or judged.
Point h
What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that the provision of services must be carried out with the victim's consent, starting from the interview process, data recording, to the handling/actions that will be taken.
Point i
What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and the use of appropriate language that is understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational, and other backgrounds that are not the same as the officers. It must be ensured that victims are served in a language understood by the victim. Lately there are increasingly more disabled/difable/disable women who become victims of violence, whether deaf, blind, or those experiencing mental retardation. What is meant by fast and simple is that the provision of services must be given immediately without unnecessary delay. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral letter. Efforts must be made so that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to their identity or case narrative.
Point k
What is meant by empathy is that officers must apply an attitude of empathy, namely the ability to place oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood, and can openly tell their problems.

What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survival, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination, and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child. (1) Repatriation of victims of violence is intended to return women and children victims of violence to their area of origin.
(2) Repatriation of women and children victims of violence is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.
(3) The Regional Government carries out the repatriation and social reintegration of women and children victims of violence in accordance with the prevailing laws and regulations.

(3) Health services specifically for children victims of violence must prioritize the best interests of the child.
(4) Women and children victims of violence have the right to health services, including:
a. Medical services
b. Medicolegal services

1. GENERAL
Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty that we must always protect because inherent in them is dignity, honor and rights as human beings that must be upheld. The human rights of children are part of human rights included in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth and development, participation and the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.
Likewise with women, from women are expected to be born children who are healthy, strong, resilient, of noble character, potential and quality. Through the role of women in the family, society and state will be born resilient generations who will continue the ideals of the nation.
As Indonesian citizens, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves according to their abilities, dignity and honor.
As assets and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development. Likewise with women, women need to be protected from acts of discrimination and from acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the dignity of women themselves, women and children often become objects, outlets for desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect and so forth.
To realize the protection of women and children, support is needed, legislation that can guarantee its implementation.
The Child Rights Convention affirms that preventive efforts must be made so that children are protected from kidnapping, smuggling and trafficking. In following up on the Child Rights Convention, the government established Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights has included the Rights of Children, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, family, society, government and the State. Child protection in all its aspects is part of National development activities, particularly in advancing national and state life.
Parents, family and society are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with obligations imposed by law. Likewise in the context of implementing child protection, the State, government and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.
Although the protection and rights of women and children have been regulated in national level legislation, because the fulfillment of constitutional rights of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of Regional Government, then in providing Protection to women and children, the Payakumbuh City Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children.
